_doc: One file per place; see places_build.py. Amounts in Egyptian pounds. The debt component, history and facts are refreshed by pipeline/fetch_egypt.py from the Ministry of Finance's quarterly Budget Sector Statistical Debt Bulletin (needs pypdf); edit wording here, not numbers.
name: Egypt
publisher: Ministry of Finance of Egypt (Debt Management Unit)
title: Egypt Debt Clock: Live Budget Sector Debt, Official Data
headline: budget sector debt
subject: The Egyptian state budget sector (central government, local administration and service authorities)
sum_note: Egypt's budget sector debt (domestic and external), from the Ministry of Finance's Budget Sector Statistical Debt Bulletin, quarter-end. Gross.
scope_note: This is the "Total Budget Sector Debt Outstanding" that Egypt's Ministry of Finance states in its quarterly Budget Sector Statistical Debt Bulletin: the domestic debt of the state budget sector plus the external debt serviced by the Ministry, converted into Egyptian pounds. The domestic part includes foreign-currency debt owed to Egyptian residents. It does not include the debt of the economic public authorities and state-owned companies, nor the Central Bank's own liabilities. Because about a quarter of the debt is in foreign currency, the pound figure moves with the exchange rate as well as with borrowing.
trend_why: We use the change over the latest twelve months rather than the last quarter because quarterly changes swing with the exchange rate and with issuance.
legend: Egypt's public debt is reported quarterly, with a lag of several months. Issuance happens in lumps at auctions and maturities, so the live number is a straight-line projection between official figures, shown here next to them.
cadence: Quarterly. The Ministry of Finance publishes a bulletin for each quarter-end with a lag of several months.
after_text: , after a lag of several months
next_update: The Ministry of Finance publishes a Budget Sector Statistical Debt Bulletin each quarter, with a lag of several months; this page re-bases to it automatically on the next daily build after it appears.

breakdown.label: Domestic budget sector debt (includes foreign-currency debt owed to Egyptian residents)
External budget sector debt (foreign-currency debt held by non-residents)

notes: Why the Ministry's bulletin: it is the Ministry of Finance's own quarterly statement of the budget sector's debt. The fetcher reads the latest bulletin and the one about a year earlier and checks that domestic plus external equals the total.
Budget sector, not general government: the measure is narrower than the IMF's general-government figure, which includes more entities, and not like-for-like with other countries' pages.
Lag: the newest bulletin is several months behind the date.

Currency: Egyptian pounds. The World Debt Clock converts them to US dollars at the US Treasury's Reporting Rates of Exchange (a quarterly official rate as of 30 September 2026; the page for the World Debt Clock shows the rate and its date).
